what: The UPS Battery Backup Calculator tells you how long a UPS or home inverter will keep your devices running on its batteries. Enter the battery voltage, capacity in Ah, number of batteries and how they are connected, the battery type and inverter efficiency, and your load in watts.
It also works backwards to find the battery you need for a target number of hours, and suggests a UPS or inverter rating in VA with headroom for safety.
uses: Know how many hours of fans and lights you get.
Check how long a desktop and router will stay on.
Find the Ah needed for a target backup time.
Pick the right VA rating for your load.
See how much longer a lithium battery lasts.
tutorial: Choose the voltage of each battery, its Ah, how many you have and whether they are in series or parallel.
Lead-acid uses about 50% of capacity, tubular 60% and lithium 90%. Choose Custom to type your own.
Most inverters and UPSs are 80–90% efficient.
Type your total watts, or press the device buttons to add typical values.
See hours and minutes, usable energy and battery current.
Type the hours you want to see the battery needed, and read the suggested inverter size.
features: Shows the bank's voltage, Ah and kWh.
Warns when high current will cut lead-acid capacity.
Ah and number of batteries needed.

example.title: Worked example: one 150 Ah battery
example.text: One 12 V 150 Ah lead-acid battery stores 1,800 Wh. Using 50% of it through an 85% efficient inverter gives 765 Wh, so a 300 W load runs for about 2 h 33 min. A lithium battery of the same size (90% usable, 90% efficient) runs it for about 4 h 52 min. A 500 VA inverter is suggested.

tips: Real loads change: fans and fridges cycle, so measured use is often lower.
Do not regularly drain lead-acid batteries below half.
Use batteries of the same type, age and size together.
Motors (fridges, pumps) need extra inverter headroom to start.
problems: Old batteries lose capacity, and lead-acid gives less at high current. Lower the usable percentage.
Use a higher system voltage (24 V or 48 V) to reduce current and cable size.
Inverter trips when the fridge starts
Motors draw up to 3 times their running watts when starting; choose a bigger inverter.
